items.source_en:
Please answer questions as honestly and completely as possible.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Have you had any recent changes to your medical history?
---Colonoscopy. Removed polyps.
---Recently diagnosed with IBS

2. On a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate your current job satisfaction?
---8

3. Have you at any time in the last 3 months experienced periods of abnormal anxiety, anger, sleeplessness, and/or irritability?
---Some sleeplessness, but only due to noisy bunkmates.

4. Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or others?
---Nothing outside of reprimanding said noisy bunkmates.

5. How would you describe your current work/life balance?
---It could be better. We don't get much vacation time, so I don't get to go home and see my wife and kid as often as I'd like, and that's been hard on us.

6. Do you have any unusual concerns about your coworkers?
---Not really. Hank's got a bit of a chip on his shoulder, but the kid seems harmless enough. He'll learn.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. 최근 병력에 변화가 있었습니까?
---대장내시경 검사. 용종 제거.
---최근 과민성 대장 증후군 진단받음

---8

3. 지난 3개월 동안 비정상적인 불안, 분노, 불면증 및/또는 짜증을 겪은 적이 있습니까?
---약간의 불면증은 있었지만, 같은 방에서 자는 동숙자가 시끄러워서 그랬을 뿐입니다.

items.source_en:
Haddie,

My friend. It was over twenty years ago when I received the first of many letters, addressed to you. It was clear you were my apartment's previous tenant, but not knowing who you were or where you moved to, I kept your things in a box. The letters, anyway. 

The packages, the bouquet of roses, the furniture - those I had to make space for. With every delivery, I began to piece together this odd and wonderful existence of yours, and imagined our lives running parallel; always at a distance, but side by side. 

It was only when the naval officer stepped to my door, and spoke the words no mother wants to hear, that I realized I needed to seek you out.

When I finally did locate your address, I did not know how to deliver that news. It was one of the hardest things I ever had to do. Yet you responded to my words with such love and gratitude that it brought me to tears. We have been friends ever since.

Twenty years and countless letters later, I am once again struggling to find the right words. I guess I'll just come out and say it. This will be my last letter to you. I am at a point in my life where I am counting the weeks. Soon, they will be days. And I do not want you to think I left you alone.

내 친구 해디.

 소포나, 꽃다발이나, 가구 같은 것들은 따로 보관해 놓았어요. 무언가 소포로 도착할 때마다 당신이라는 신기하고도 독특한 존재의 조각이 하나씩 맞춰지는 느낌이었달까, 마치 저마다의 삶이 항상 닿지 않는 거리에서 나란히 달려가는 것과 같았어요.

 언젠가 해군 장교가 찾아온 적 있어요. 그리고 엄마라면 절대 듣고 싶지 않은 말을 들었을 때 비로소 당신을 찾아내야 한다는 걸 깨달았죠.

 결국 당신의 주소를 찾아냈을 때 이 소식을 어떻게 전달 해야 할지 몰랐어요. 제가 해야 했던 일 중에 가장 힘든 일이었답니다. 하지만 당신은 제 말에 엄청난 사랑과 감사를 표했죠. 그리고 저는 눈물이 나버렸죠. 그때부터 저흰 친구가 되었잖아요.

20년 간 그리고 셀 수 없는 편지들, 한 번 더 어떤 말을 해야 할지 모르는 상황이 와버렸네요. 단도직입적으로 말할게요. 이게 제 마지막 편지가 될 거예요. 제 남은 시간은 몇 주 안 돼요. 곧 며칠이 되겠죠. 제가 당신을 버렸다고 생각하지 말아 주세요.

사실 정반대예요. 저는 언제나 당신과 함께할 거예요. 당신의 영혼 속에서, 가슴 속에서. 당신 20년 동안 보낸 모든 편지, 소포, 그리고 사랑이 그 증거랍니다.
